newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool prices seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool prices seen rising.

text.p: Australian wool prices are expected to continue to firm at auctions in Sydney, Melbourne and Fremantle, with about 99,000 bales on offer, Wesfarmers Dalgety said in its weekly market preview.
This weeks selection is expected to have the same firming effect on the market, as last week's, despite another large offering, Wesfarmers said.

The smaller rostered sales for the next three weeks will put buyers under pressure to complete orders, particularly for those orders generated over the break. This is also supporting the upturn, it said.
The eastern market indicator rose 7.0 cents to 626 cents a kg clean and the western indicator rose 4.0 cents to 593 cents.

"Coupled with Wool International's sales of just over 200,000 bales of stockpile last week, including sales for delivery in the December 1997 quarter, this large volume of trade clearances at higher price levels provides a very encouraging basis for the balance of this season, the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said.
